findings.description: AWS access key and secret key are hardcoded in plaintext within the instance user_data script, which is stored in the EC2 instance metadata and Terraform state, exposing long-term IAM credentials to anyone with access to the instance metadata service, console, or state file.
The security group allows inbound SSH (port 22) from 0.0.0.0/0, exposing the management interface to the entire internet and enabling brute-force or credential-stuffing attacks.

The security group allows inbound HTTP (port 80) from 0.0.0.0/0. While this may be intended for a public web server, combined with unrestricted SSH it broadens overall attack surface and should be reviewed for necessity of full public access.
The EBS volume does not set encrypted = true, meaning data at rest on this disk is stored unencrypted, risking exposure if the underlying storage is compromised or the volume/snapshot is shared.
The snapshot is taken from an unencrypted volume and has no encryption configured, so backup data at rest remains unencrypted and could be exposed if the snapshot is shared or made public.

findings.issue_category: missing encryption and public access controls
findings.description: The S3 bucket used to store VPC flow logs has no server-side encryption configuration, no bucket policy restricting access, and no public access block, potentially allowing unauthorized read/write access to sensitive network flow log data; force_destroy also allows irreversible deletion of the bucket and its contents.
map_public_ip_on_launch is set to true, automatically assigning public IPs to any instance launched in this subnet, increasing exposure of instances to the internet.
map_public_ip_on_launch is set to true, automatically assigning public IPs to any instance launched in this subnet, increasing exposure of instances to the internet even if not currently used.
